intro.text: On January 1, 2025, we changed our corporate name from Gray Television, Inc. to Gray Media, Inc. We will not distinguish between our prior and current corporate name and will refer to our current corporate name throughout this Annual Report. As such, in this Annual Report, unless otherwise indicated or the context otherwise requires, the words “Gray,” “Gray Media,” “the Company,” “we,” “us,” and “our” refer to Gray Media, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries. Unless otherwise indicated, all station rank, in-market share and television household data herein are derived from reports prepared by The Nielsen Company US, LLC (“Nielsen”) and/or Comscore, Inc. (“Comscore”).

lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: For the year ended December 31, 2025, our CBS-affiliated channels accounted for approximately 37% of total revenue; our NBC-affiliated channels accounted for approximately 27% of total revenue; our FOX-affiliated channels accounted for approximately 14% of total revenue; and our ABC-affiliated channels accounted for approximately 11% of total revenue.

During the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023 approximately 17%, 20% and 20%, respectively, of our broadcast advertising revenue (excluding political advertising revenue) was obtained from advertising sales to automotive customers.
For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, we derived approximately 1% and 14%, respectively, of our total revenue from political broadcast advertisers.

Approximately 26%, 23%, and 27% of our Core Advertising Revenue was derived from advertising sales to customers in the services sector for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.
Approximately 17%, 20%, and 20% of our Core Advertising Revenue was derived from advertising sales to automotive customers for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.

Although our revenues can be affected by changes within our customer base, we believe this risk is in part mitigated due to the fact that no one customer accounted for in excess of 5% of our broadcast advertising revenue in any of these periods.
Because broadcast stations rely on advertising revenues, they are sensitive to cyclical changes in the economy.
Broadcast stations like ours rely on advertising revenue and are therefore sensitive to cyclical changes in the economy.
Affiliated stations depend on the performance of the network programs to attract viewers.
Advertising revenues comprise the primary source of revenues for our stations.
Our main source of revenue is the sale of advertising time and space.
We rely on technology and data owned or controlled by us or our third-party service providers in substantially all aspects of our business operations.
Our ability to service our significant financial obligations depends on our ability to generate significant cash flow.
We are a holding company with no material independent assets or operations and we depend on our subsidiaries for cash.

While we have paid dividends to holders of our common stock on a quarterly basis since the beginning of 2021, any future payments of dividends will depend on our financial condition, results of operations, cash flows and such other factors as our Board of Directors deems relevant.
Our primary sources of liquidity are cash on hand, cash flows from operations and borrowing capacity under our Revolving Credit Facility and revolving accounts receivable securitization facility.
